Where it began

Ben Curran was born in Northampton on 7 June 1996 and grew up in Zimbabwe. Cricket ran through the house. His father, Kevin Curran, played international cricket for Zimbabwe, and Ben was the second of the Curran boys. His brothers Tom and Sam went on to play for England, which must have made games in the back garden a fairly serious business.

Ben took the English route first. He played for the MCC Young Cricketers and turned out for Nottinghamshire's second team before joining Northamptonshire, the county of his birthplace.

The player

His Twenty20 debut for Northamptonshire came in August 2018, and a few weeks later he played his first first-class match, against Durham. Back in Zimbabwe he batted for the Southern Rocks in the Logan Cup in two seasons.

Zimbabwe called him up at the end of 2024, first for the one-day side against Afghanistan, and his first game ended early in the rain with Ben on 15. Days later, against the same opponents, he began his Test career with a bright 68 off 74 balls. In February 2025 he made an unbeaten 118 against Ireland at Harare Sports Club, his first one-day international hundred, to set up a nine-wicket win.

By November 2026 he had played 9 Tests, scoring 537 runs at 33.56. His best was 121, his first Test hundred, and he had added a fifty and taken 9 catches.

What made him special

Curran is a left-hander who is happy to play his shots, as that 68 from 74 balls on debut showed. He reached international cricket after years in county and domestic cricket on two continents, and he batted like a man who knew what the chance was worth.

Tom and Sam found their way into England colours. Ben took the longer road, through second-team cricket, county cricket and the Logan Cup, and when the call finally came he was ready for it.

Away from the middle

Few families can match the Currans for international caps. A father who played for Zimbabwe, two brothers who played for England, and then Ben in Zimbabwe colours as well. Between them they cover a fair part of the cricketing map, from Harare to Northampton and beyond.

And finally

His one-day career began with 15 runs and a rain cloud. Within two months he had a hundred to his name. Some players need a while to settle; Ben Curran just needed the weather to clear.
